claims.claim: Intersect requests 1,193,000 ADA, stated as $298,250, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The proposal allocates 256,000 ADA to WP1, 832,000 ADA to WP2, and 105,000 ADA to WP3, totaling 1,193,000 ADA.
WP2 will fund the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group to support protocol governance and evolution.
WP3 will establish a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027 with conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal says all expenditure will be fully accounted for and unspent funds will be returned to the Cardano treasury.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation, audited results, and audit materials.
The proposal states the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit at submission and links to the relevant governance action.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverables, controls, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

Intersect will administer the funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with listed TRSC and PSSC addresses, named oversight entities, permission thresholds, audit references, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect Technical Steering Committee support across community technical coordination, protocol governance, and technical review, with stated smart-contract-based treasury administration, oversight, audit, reporting, and return-of-unused-funds commitments.
